analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-buffer-overflow is caused by missing edge-boundary handling in bink_decode_plane() when decoding SCALED_BLOCK/FILL_BLOCK near frame borders. For chroma planes, bw/bh are computed with ceil ((width+15)>>4,(height+15)>>4), so a 16x16 fill can be issued for a partial edge block. The code calls fill_block_tab[0](dst, v, stride, 16), which maps to fill_block16_c() and writes 16 bytes per row for 16 rows unconditionally. At right/bottom edges this overruns the allocated plane buffer (ASan shows write exactly past a 512-byte allocation).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Via ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_BINK_fuzzer, crafted BINK bitstream drives decode_frame()->bink_decode_plane() into SCALED_BLOCK then sub-type FILL_BLOCK on an edge macroblock where remaining valid pixels are <16 in width and/or height. Because bink_decode_plane does not clip block dimensions before calling the 16x16 fill primitive, memset writes beyond frame->data plane allocation returned by ff_get_buffer/fuzz_get_buffer2, triggering heap OOB write.
